key_concepts: Oviparous animals lay eggs that develop outside the mother's body
Viviparous animals give birth to live young that develop inside the mother's body
Birds, reptiles, fish, and amphibians are examples of oviparous animals
Mammals such as dogs, cats, and humans are examples of viviparous animals
Gestation period is the time a pregnant animal carries developing young inside its body
Incubation period is the time it takes for an egg to hatch
Viviparous embryos receive nourishment from the mother through a placenta
Oviparous embryos receive nourishment from the yolk sac inside the egg
Oviparous animals often produce many young or have protective shells for embryos
Viviparous animals can focus care and nourishment on one or few young
Life cycles include stages from birth to death and vary among organisms
